data.text/markdown:
xs_si_mom_composite · tuning around version B, overnight

The standard setting is version B: the shipped rules on the 2000 most traded stocks (RESEARCH_LOG §13.5). A first search that changed all 33 knobs at random found nothing better: almost every random setting carries several bad choices at once, and 100 points cannot cover 33 knobs. This version searches around version B instead, in three stages, and then checks whether its best setting would really have done better without knowing the future. One click runs the whole night (set the time budget in step 2; 8 hours by default):
  1. Each knob alone: every listed value of every knob, everything else at version B (about 140 backtests, about an hour).
  2. Combine the winners: start from version B and add the single changes that helped, best first, keeping each one only if the combination scores higher still.
  3. Small random combinations of 2 to 5 changes around version B, until only the time the checks need is left.
  4. The checks (about 45 minutes), then the verdict.
Everything is saved as it runs. If the night is interrupted, click again: settings already backtested are read back, not rerun. Keep the Mac awake, for example by running caffeinate -i in a terminal. The last step, the reserved months, is read by hand, once.

1 · The data

  • One panel of every stock the widest universe (the 2000 most traded, any price) held since 2022: daily prices from mid-2019, FINRA short interest, SEC share counts and profitability, and sectors. Narrower universes are cut from it. It loads from the cache in var/ (the first load takes about 10 minutes).
  • The search window is 2022-01 → 2025-12. Before mid-2020 the database holds only about 500 stocks, and momentum needs a year of history. 2026-01 → today is reserved for the last step.
  • The check below rebuilds version B with this notebook's code and compares it with the shipped strategy. 0 means it trades exactly the strategy.

Loaded: 2,206 stocks, 2019-07-01 → 2026-10-16, 10 universe formations. Check: the largest difference between this notebook's version B and the shipped signals() is 0.0e+00 (identical: the knobs below change the real strategy).

2 · What to search

All 33 knobs are listed below with version B's value and every value the search tries. Untick a knob to keep it at version B. Stop-losses (group "stops"; version B has none):
  • A long is sold when its close falls k daily volatilities below its entry (or below its best close since entry, with "best close"). A short is covered when its close rises that far. The volatility is the stock's own: the standard deviation of its daily returns over the 20 sessions before the entry. Example: a stock that moves about 2% a day, k = 5: the stop sits 10% away.
  • Like every decision of this strategy, a stop is read at the close and traded at the next open. A real stop order would fill during the day it is hit, often a little better.
  • A stopped stock is not bought (or shorted) again until its rank has left the entry zone once.
The account size is a knob too, up to $100k. Every order pays its own costs:
  • commission at its real size ($0.005 a share, at least $1);
  • half the spread (about 1-3 bp by how much the stock trades, never below one cent);
  • market impact, which grows with the order against the stock's daily trading (volatility × √(order ÷ daily dollar volume)).
A bigger account pays less commission per dollar but moves thin stocks more. If your account is fixed, untick account: every setting then uses the amount chosen below. Kept fixed, never searched: the borrow-fee model (0.5% a year, 3% above 10% of the shares shorted, 10% above 20%), the cost model above, and market-on-open fills. They describe what trading costs, not choices. What "better" means (the score, all against equal-weight buy-and-hold of version B's 2000 stocks, so every universe is judged on one yardstick):
  • robust (recommended): each half-year's alpha, mean minus half their spread. A steady edge beats one lucky stretch.
  • alpha: the yearly return beyond what the book's market exposure explains.
  • alpha ratio: alpha per unit of the book's own stock-specific risk.
A setting must trade at least 20 times a year to be picked.

3 · Version B, the setting to beat

The shipped rules on the top 2000, run on the search window (2022-01 → 2025-12) with your account. Every metric below is also computed for every setting the search tries.

4 · The overnight run

  • Saved as it runs in studies/, under a name built from the searched knobs, the score, your account and this code's version. Change any of them and a fresh search starts; click again with the same choices and it resumes.
  • Stages 1 and 3 never look at results (a fixed list, and random draws from a fixed seed). Stage 2 does, so the walk-forward check reruns it on the past only, half-year by half-year. That tests exactly the rule that picks the winner.
  • The checks run straight after the search, inside the same click.

5 · What the search found

Stage 1: each knob alone

Every dot is version B with one knob changed to one of its values. Right of the line is a better score than version B, left a worse one. Hover for the value. A knob whose dots all sit near the line hardly matters; one with dots far to the right is worth a look, but a single dot far out on one value is often luck.

data.text/markdown:
6 · The checks: is the pick really better?

The pick is the best-scoring setting on the whole search window among version B, every stage-1 and stage-3 setting, and the stage-2 combination. The verdict needs A to F to pass.
  • A walk-forward. For every half-year from 2024 on, the whole rule (stage 2 on the past half-years, then the best on the past) picks a setting; the next half-year is traded with it. Passes: the stitched record beats version B with P(really better) ≥ 0.80.
  • B overfitting (PBO). Over every split of the half-years into two halves: how often does the best setting on one half land in the bottom half on the other? Passes: below 0.5 (0.5 is picking blindly).
  • C luck. Does the pick beat the same book on randomly swapped stocks of similar liquidity? Passes: it beats 95% of them.
  • D neighbours. Do the settings one listed value away on any knob keep the gain, or is it one lucky point? Passes: their median alpha is above version B's.
  • E costs. Fills 0.5% worse, every cost doubled, whole shares. Passes: alpha above 0 every time, and at least version B's with the worse fills.
  • F missing stocks. 5% of the stocks removed at random, three times. Passes: alpha above 0 each time, on average at least version B's.
  • G account size (information only): the pick at every account size up to $100k.

data.text/markdown:
7 · The reserved months (2026-01 → today)

The search and the checks never saw these months. Read them once, when you are done tuning. Looking, changing a knob and looking again turns them into one more search window. It is a short stretch: a gap of a few points a year between two settings is noise here (RESEARCH_LOG §13.5). Fair warning: version B's own 2026 has been looked at before (RESEARCH_LOG §13.5, and while this notebook was built: alpha about −2% a year). For a new setting these months are unseen; for version B they are not.
